questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to explore new cultures, but I didn't want a culture that was too far from the danish, which would take a lot of getting used to. The French roots in Montreal makes the culture a lot like the european which was very nice. Also I've always wanted to study at a North American university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. You can find almost everything on McGills website.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got a lot of emails with information. In the intro-weekend I was able to ask returning students different questions I had.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found it through airbnb which is very easy, but a bit more expensive than for example Facebook marketplace.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The downtown campus is super central in the city, so it is not a problem at all living off campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I don't really remember but I only think you need to registrer for courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You get emails containing all the information you need. There was also different zoom meeting you could attend which went through the registration process.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be ready when they open for registration. Don't worry if you don't get all the classes you want, you will be put on a waitlist and most likely get the class anyway. There is a drop/add deadline a week or two into the semester which means you could get the class a little after the semester starts.

questions.answer: Very easy. A lot like the european.

questions.answer: I didn't really find any challenges.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They are very outgoing compared to Denmark.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Bring/buy warm clothes for the winter
Learn a little bit of French if possible
Walk the city or get a bike membership rather than taking public transport

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure you get a RAMQ card so you don't have to pay for their insurance.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Personal development

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: No established groups in the courses.
